title: Asynchronous Iteration
learning_outcomes: Describe Iterators and iterables and explain how it relates to Asynchronous Iteration.
Demonstrate Async iterators in a small Node.js example and predict the observable result.
Test a failure, boundary, lifecycle, or version-compatibility case involving for await...of.

content.intro: Asynchronous Iteration is part of asynchronous programming. This lesson connects Iterators and iterables, Async iterators, for await...of to a concrete Node.js example. Focus on the behavior you can observe, the assumptions the API makes, and one failure or boundary case.
content.why_it_matters: Promises and async/await express asynchronous completion and error propagation; they do not automatically make CPU-bound work parallel. Test successful completion, rejection, timeout/cancellation, partial failure, and cleanup.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Promises and async/await express asynchronous completion and error propagation; they do not automatically make CPU-bound work parallel. Use await with try/catch, run independent tasks concurrently with bounded concurrency, and make cancellation/retries explicit.

async function* numbers() { yield 1; yield 2; }
for await (const value of numbers()) console.log(value);

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety note
content_blocks.text: Teaching baseline: use a supported Node.js LTS release (Node.js 24 LTS as checked on 2026-10-13). The official releases page lists Node.js 26 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS. Some advanced APIs, flags, permission behavior, embedded SQLite capabilities, module-loader hooks, and TypeScript integration are version-sensitive; verify the exact installed runtime. The Node.js 22 runtime available in the build-check environment is used only for syntax checks. This example is for learning and static validation, not for executing untrusted learner code inside CodeLeaf.

content.task: Create or inspect a small Node.js example for Asynchronous Iteration. Include at least one listed subtopic, document the expected result, and verify a normal case plus a boundary or failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates a named lesson concept, rather than only mentioning the title.
Expected output or observable behavior is documented and reproducible.
At least one invalid, empty, timeout, resource, or failure case is handled or explained.
The solution does not put secrets in source code and does not execute untrusted code inside the production API process.

common_mistakes.problem: Awaiting independent tasks one by one or launching unlimited concurrent operations.
common_mistakes.why: The code may pass a simple demonstration yet fail with real inputs, resource limits, timing, or runtime differences.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose sequential or concurrent flow deliberately and cap work according to resource limits.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its runtime, dependencies, input assumptions, or cleanup behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Node.js APIs and surrounding ecosystem tools have explicit version, trust, and resource boundaries.
common_mistakes.fix: State the environment and dependency assumptions, then rerun the example from a clean starting state.
